_comment: Sources for the security intel Reader (scripts/papers/security.py). NOT a publishing channel — nothing here can write a post. These are the PRACTITIONER security sources: advisories, attack writeups, defensive tooling and standards. The security PAPERS live in the papers Reader's cs.CR bucket instead; this file deliberately contains no arXiv. Every entry was fetched on 2026-10-04 and the item count and newest-item date below are measured, not assumed.

feeds.note: The single highest-signal source in this file. Prompt injection, agent exploitation, data exfiltration through LLM tooling, usually with a working proof of concept. 2026-10-04: 232 items, newest 2026-09-30.
Security research house. Not AI-only, so the keyword profile does the filtering. 2026-10-04: 20 items, newest 2026-10-02.
HIGH VOLUME (873 items) and mostly not security. Carried only because HF is where supply-chain incidents on the model hub get written up. The keyword profile must do real work here.
All of NIST, not just AI. Standards and framework updates; slow but occasionally load-bearing. 2026-10-04: 40 items, newest 2026-09-28.
The evaluation harness AISI builds its safety evals on. Release notes name new eval types. 2026-10-04: 10 items, newest 2026-10-02 — actively developed.
Scanner for MCP server vulnerabilities — tool poisoning, rug pulls, cross-origin escalation. 2026-10-04: 10 items, newest 2026-09-29.
New probe classes are the interesting part; the version bumps are not. 2026-10-04: 10 items, newest 2026-09-09.
MCP is a live attack surface and this is where its reference servers change. 2026-10-04: 10 items, newest 2026-08-31.
Defensive tooling. 2026-10-04: 10 items, newest 2026-08-14 — slow but alive.
The adversarial-ML threat matrix. Updates are rare but each one means a new documented technique. 2026-10-04: 10 items, newest 2026-04-30.

feeds.scopeNote: Fetches fine (3 items) but the newest release is 2024-11-18 — 23 months old. The Top 10 is a document that is revised every year or two, so a releases feed for it is silent almost always. Kept as a record of the decision; revisit if a 2027 edition lands.
Fetches fine (10 items) but the newest release is 2025-05-19, 17 months old. Treat as abandoned until proven otherwise.
No feed; would need the HTML adapter pointed at a page whose structure has not been checked. Left out of scope rather than guessed at.

The obvious gap in this file: real CVEs against torch, transformers, vllm, gradio and friends. The HTML page is a search UI, not a feed. GitHub's GraphQL securityAdvisories API would do it properly but needs a token and an adapter. Worth building; not guessed at here.
